chapter: Learning the trade in Los Angeles
title: Learning to arrange, Ellington records, and Dancer's gambling
summary: Parker Berry taught him arranging; they played Ellington arrangements, and Dancer gambled away the payroll.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you remember what you first arranged. What sort of things would you be doing? Arrangements of popular tunes or would you be doming up with originals?
Well we had originals. We had quite a few originals. And then we would do pops
too. I don't remember what the first.....
I wondered what sort of things you broke in on ?

Well a lot of them were Duke's. Because Duke at that time was making hits one right after another. I remember Duke was in California when they first heard the play back to 'It don't mean a thing if it ain't got the Swing'. Because all of his members Sonny Greer and all of them put a nickel in the juke box. They all got in this restaurant where this record was on the juke box and they, they kept it going for hours playing that one record, 'It don't mean a thing if it ain't got that Swing'.
Now we are up to about '32.

Yes. I remember when they, it was nice to see how they reacted to their own song as far as I was concerned. So we were making arrangements like that and everything else that Duke did. And then we made pop song too. And we made originals. I wish I could remember what the first thing I did was.
Anyway, Now Parker Berry, he did most of the arranging?
But you begin to contribute too?

Yes, after you know you learn more and more and then you venture out to do things more than you would. So as we went on it started taking effect. And we ended up with a pretty good band with Earl. But only one thing about Earl, he's a big gambler.

A lot of times he'd gamble our salary you know and that's why we all left him, eventually. Because many times pay day would come and he'd shot it all up the night before in Hollywood somewhere. But it was a good band though.
